'''Gérard Vergnaud''' (8 February 1933 &ndash; 6 June 2021) was a French mathematician, philosopher, educator, and psychologist. He earned his doctorate from the International Center for Genetic [[Epistemology]] in Geneva under the [[doctoral advisor|supervision]] of [[Jean Piaget]]. Vergnaud was a [[professor emeritus]] of the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] in Paris, where he was a researcher in mathematics. Among his most significant work has been the development of the [[Theory of Conceptual Fields]], which describes how children develop an understanding of mathematics.<ref>Grossi, Gabriel Pilar [http://revistaescola.abril.com.br/matematica/fundamentos/todos-perdem-quando-nao-usamos-pesquisa-pratica-427238.shtml "Gérard Vergnaud: Todos perdem quando a pesquisa não é colocada em prática"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605080017/http://revistaescola.abril.com.br/matematica/fundamentos/todos-perdem-quando-nao-usamos-pesquisa-pratica-427238.shtml |date=5 June 2016 }} Published by Magazine Escola, 23 October 2010, accessed 29 January 2011.</ref>

Gérard Vergnaud graduated from [[HEC Paris]] in 1956 and from the [[University of Geneva]] in 1968.<ref>[https://www.amq.math.ca/wp-content/uploads/bulletin/vol61/no4/03-hommage-gvergnaud.pdf L’AMQ se souvient]</ref>
